clue.text: Pellets obtained with US money, stolen

blocks.note: bucks is American slang for dollars
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: Someone buys ammunition with stolen American dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is American slang for dollars, and hot goods are stolen ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is the coarse lead shot loaded into shotgun cartridges for hunting deer and similar game.

clue.text: Blue drink

blocks.note: first meaning: sad, low in spirits
second meaning: to swallow a drink in one go

explanation.walkthrough: Blue here is a mood, not a colour; and the drink is a verb, as in knocking a pint back in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or depressed is a synonym for blue, and to swallow quickly in one go is the verb sense.

clue.text: A good place to live without showing respect

definitions.note: a noun for the act of showing respect

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the place to live wraps around the other letters

blocks.note: where one lives
taken as written
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A homeless person, lacking a decent place to live, gets no respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but it means outside: HOME goes round A G, giving HOMAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or tribute paid to someone, which is the act of displaying regard or deference.

clue.text: Fatty alcoholic drink is hard to get

blocks.note: stout is a dark heavy beer
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rich drink that is hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty alcoholic drink' reads as one phrase, but Fatty alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoutish means somewhat stout, that is rather plump or tubby, a mild word for overweight.

clue.text: The things people say about you when you're late!

definitions.text: The things people say about you when you're late!

blocks.clueFragment: The things people say about you when you're late!
blocks.note: surface reading: the grumbles from those kept waiting by a latecomer
setter's reading: late means dead, so these are the published tributes after death

explanation.surface: The muttering of colleagues when you turn up behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: Late is the trick: not tardy but deceased, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obituaries are newspaper notices recounting the life of someone recently deceased, which is what 'the late' signals.

clue.text: US agency managed to split skulls!

indicators.note: splitting something means getting inside it, so one word goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
ran a business means managed it

explanation.surface: American spies manage to crack heads open.
explanation.walkthrough: The split need not be in the middle: the inserted word can go anywhere inside the agency's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Crania is the Latin plural of cranium, the bony case of the head enclosing the brain.

clue.text: My US car number on the front shows independence!

indicators.note: the later words are placed in front of the first one, so the clue's order is changed

blocks.note: auto is American for a car
No. is the abbreviation for number
taken as written

explanation.surface: Owning a car with my own number plate gives me freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: My comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because the car and number go on its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Autonomy is self-government or freedom to act on one's own, a close synonym of independence.

clue.text: Stop raising putting central heating in boats!

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up
putting one thing in another places it inside, as the word in later says

blocks.note: to stay is to stop or remain
CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: An order not to install central heating in sailing craft.
explanation.walkthrough: STAY read upwards is YATS, and CH goes into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Yachts are sailing or motor vessels used for racing or pleasure cruising, so a specific kind of boat.

clue.text: Volunteers to return sombre tunic

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
drab means dull and sombre

explanation.surface: Volunteers come back in a dull uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabard is a sleeveless tunic, once worn by knights over armour and by heralds bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Endlessly asking to see film

indicators.note: without ends, so the word loses both its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on asking to watch a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Film is not a movie here but a thin covering layer, as on custard.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin is a thin layer or coating over a surface, which is also a film in its older sense.

clue.text: Someone doing a balancing act?

blocks.note: surface reading: a circus performer on a tightrope
setter's reading: balancing the books, making debits and credits agree

explanation.surface: A tightrope walker or juggler performing at the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: The balancing is of ledgers, not of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An accountant keeps and checks financial records, whose job includes making the books balance at the year end.

clue.text: Taking a little time, seek to be modest

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the second word surrounds the first

blocks.note: to chase is to pursue or seek
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice to take things slowly when pursuing someone, and stay decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little time' is just T, the short form of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained in conduct, especially sexually, which overlaps with modest in the sense of decorous.

clue.text: Extremely sweet arsenic concoction with tea in it

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the poison's letters are blended into a new order
with something in it means holding it inside, as the words that follow spell out

blocks.note: taken as written
cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A poisoner's sickly brew, laced into someone's cup.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (or char) is old British slang for tea, from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharine means excessively sweet or sugary, literally of sugar and figuratively of sentimentality.

clue.text: Decorate a raced vessel

blocks.note: to trim a dress or tree is to decorate it
taken as written
ran fast means raced

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up a boat that took part in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimaran is a boat with three parallel hulls, a type of sailing craft or vessel.

clue.text: Admits one may be punched on a train

definitions.note: the wording printed on the item, standing for the thing itself

definitions.text: may be punched on a train

blocks.note: first meaning: the words printed on a pass for a single entry

blocks.clueFragment: may be punched on a train
blocks.note: second meaning: what a guard clips a hole in during a rail journey

explanation.surface: A passenger confesses they might get assaulted during a rail journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admits one' is not a confession but the wording printed on the item; punching is the conductor's clipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail pass is checked by the conductor, who traditionally clipped a hole in it to show it had been used.

clue.text: Then leap out of jumbo?

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the two words are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to jump clear of a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo looks like the aircraft, but it is the famous circus animal the jet was named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was the name of a famous huge London Zoo animal and became a nickname for any large pachyderm.

clue.text: Excellent couple of fellows quitting church office

indicators.note: those who are quitting leave, so these letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written
F is short for fellow, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two good men resign their posts in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church office' reads as one thing, but church gives CH and office loses its FF.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means of very good quality, select or superior, especially of food.

clue.text: Engineer stands still, enraptured

blocks.note: CE, civil engineer, here written the other way round
something that stands still is static, not moving

explanation.surface: A delighted engineer is rooted to the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual abbreviation for an engineer is CE (civil engineer) or E; the clue needs EC and gives no signal for the turnaround, so it is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy or delight, which is to be carried away or enraptured.

clue.text: Susie opened front door and emerged

indicators.note: opening something up breaks it apart, so the name's letters are rearranged
the front of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the name taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: Susie opened the front door and stepped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front door' looks like a single thing, but front picks the first letter of door.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come or flow out of somewhere, so issued means came out or emerged.

clue.text: Hurts Les badly, lacking pity

indicators.note: badly suggests things done wrongly, so the letters end up in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone harms a man called Les without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means without compassion or mercy, ruth being an old word for sorrow and pity.

clue.text: No longer bound to take auntie dancing in it

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it within, so the answer sits inside the words that follow
completes the phrase take in, saying the run of letters is contained within the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, dropping the first and the tail

explanation.surface: Someone freed from obligations takes an elderly aunt out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie dancing' looks like an anagram, but no letters are shuffled: the answer runs straight through the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied means unfastened or released from ties, so something once bound is now loose and free.

clue.text: When Sister Elizabeth goes to find help

indicators.note: the queen goes, meaning she leaves, so her letters are taken away

blocks.note: as in the sense of while or when
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A nun leaves her convent in search of aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister Elizabeth' looks like a nun's name; Elizabeth is ER, which is removed from SISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist someone is to give them help or aid, so the two verbs are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Means business

blocks.note: first meaning: the means or instrumentality by which something is done
second meaning: a firm providing a service, such as a travel firm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Means business' reads as being serious; it is two separate nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency is both the action or medium through which a result is achieved and a company acting for clients.

clue.text: Treasury supply Head Office with employment

blocks.note: a store is a supply kept for later
HO is the abbreviation for head office
use means employment, as in employing a tool

explanation.surface: The Treasury provides a head office with jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Treasury looks like the government department, but it is a place where treasure is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is literally a place where valuables are kept, which makes it a kind of storage building or depository.

clue.text: Final artiste in strip show

indicators.note: final points to the last letter, so only that one is kept
in means placed inside, so the single letter sits within the other word

blocks.note: a bar is a narrow strip, as of metal
its last letter

explanation.surface: The closing act of a striptease performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip show' looks like one phrase; strip is BAR and show is the definition, as in bearing a scar.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear can mean to carry or display visibly, as when a document bears a signature or a face bears marks.

clue.text: Raised by Black, looking angry

blocks.note: B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
seeing red means being angry

explanation.surface: Someone brought up by a cross, scowling figure named Black.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means brought up or reared, as a child or animal is raised from birth.

clue.text: Write name on flag

blocks.note: to pen a letter is to write it
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a name on a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow pointed banner, historically carried on a knight's lance.

clue.text: Old and feeble pet cried to be put out

indicators.note: being put out means being disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An aged, frail pet whimpered when it was put outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone or something worn out and weakened by age, infirm and dilapidated.
